- The right square can move vertically between rows 39 and 54 (at col 44).

Wait, I can move the right square down to row 44 by pressing DOWN. Then the left square moves from row 14 to row 19. Then I press UP, and the left square moves from row 19 to row 14, and the right square moves from row 44 to row 39. This just undoes the DOWN.
The problem is that both squares move together vertically, so I can't change the relative vertical distance between them. The left square is 25 rows above the right square (14 vs 39), and this distance remains constant.

Wait, let me re-check. Earlier, the left square was at row 9 and the right square was at row 39. The distance was 30 rows (6 steps). But now the distance is 25 rows (5 steps). How did the distance change?

- After LEFT: left at (39, 14), right at (44, 44). Distance: 5 rows.
- After UP: left at (34, 14), right at (39, 44). Distance: 5 rows.
- After 3x UP: left at (19, 14), right at (39, 44). Distance: 20 rows.
Wait, the distance changed from 5 to 20 rows! This means the squares DON'T always move together vertically. The left square moved 3 steps (15 rows), but the right square didn't move.
So the rule is: the left square can move up even when the right square is blocked. But the right square can't move up when the left square is blocked.
This is asymmetric! Let me re-examine:
- When both squares can move, they both move.
- When the right square is blocked but the left square can move, the left square moves and the right square stays.
- When the left square is blocked but the right square can move, both stay (left blocks right).

This explains how the left square got to row 9 while the right square was at row 39. The left square moved up 3 steps (from 34 to 19) while the right square was blocked at row 39.
